documents.title: H&P - Admission, Sepsis Secondary to Urinary Source
lines: HPI:
87 yo female brought to ED at 01:40 by daughter for 1 day of confusion, decreased oral intake, and shaking chills.
Daughter reports patient normally independent and oriented; on arrival confused, oriented to self only, GCS 13.
Two days of urinary frequency and suprapubic discomfort per daughter. No cough, no diarrhea, no abdominal pain reported.
Last seen at baseline yesterday morning when she made her own breakfast and walked to the mailbox.
No falls, no head strike. No recent hospitalization or procedures.
Past Medical History:
Hypertension, type 2 diabetes (diet controlled), osteoarthritis, prior UTI x2 in past year, mild diastolic dysfunction.
No prior CKD, no dialysis.
Home Medications:
Amlodipine 5 mg daily, lisinopril 10 mg daily, atorvastatin 20 mg nightly, acetaminophen 650 mg PRN, vitamin D 1000 units daily.
Allergies: penicillin - rash in childhood, tolerates cephalosporins.
Social:
Lives alone in single level home, daughter visits daily. No tobacco, no alcohol. Uses cane outdoors only.
ROS: Limited by mental status. Per daughter: positive for chills, weakness, urinary frequency. Negative for chest pain, vomiting, rash.
ED Course and Vitals:
Temperature 37.9 C at triage; WBC 11,200.
Respiratory rate 30; SpO2 88% on RA, placed on 6L NC with SpO2 93%.
Initial BP 92/54, HR 112, irregular but no known AF, glucose 168.
Lactate 4.2 mmol/L at 02:10, 3.6 mmol/L repeat at 05:30.
Received 2.5 L normal saline bolus (30 mL/kg); BP after bolus 86/48, MAP 61.
Post-bolus vitals at 04:45: HR 118, BP 88/50, RR 26, T 38.9 C.
Norepinephrine discussed by ED team for MAP 64; held after additional fluid with MAP 68.
Ceftriaxone 1 g IV given at 04:30 as the only antibiotic dose.
Physical Exam:
Gen: frail elderly female, ill appearing, arousable but slow to respond.
HEENT: dry mucous membranes, no scleral icterus.
Neck: supple, no JVD, no lymphadenopathy.
Cardiac: tachycardic, regular, no murmur, cap refill 3 sec.
Pulm: tachypneic, accessory muscle use mild, lungs clear bilaterally, no crackles.
Abd: soft, mild suprapubic tenderness, no rebound, no CVA tenderness.
Ext: warm, no edema, no cellulitis, no sacral ulcer.
Neuro: oriented to self only, follows simple commands, no focal deficit, no neck stiffness.
Skin: no rash, no petechiae.
Labs:
Creatinine 2.6 mg/dL (baseline 0.9 mg/dL); platelets 84,000.
Na 133, K 4.4, HCO3 18, BUN 38, glucose 168, AST 32, ALT 28, T bili 1.1, INR 1.2.
Urinalysis with large leukocyte esterase and more than 50 WBC per high power field.
Blood culture x2 and urine culture drawn at 02:20 before antibiotics.
Imaging:
CXR portable: no consolidation, no effusion, mild bibasilar atelectasis.
Renal US: no hydronephrosis, no post void residual of significance (40 mL).
Assessment:
87 yo F with sepsis, urinary source, with AKI, thrombocytopenia, hypoxemia, and acute encephalopathy.
Plan:
Admit to stepdown, sepsis pathway. Continue IV fluids 100 mL/hr NS, reassess volume status q4h.
Trend lactate q6h until normalized. Follow culture data, narrow antibiotic when susceptibilities return.
Hold lisinopril and amlodipine given hypotension and AKI. Hold metformin - not on home list.
O2 to keep SpO2 greater than 92%, wean as tolerated.
Strict I/O, foley deferred, bladder scan q6h.
Delirium precautions, avoid benzodiazepines, family at bedside, mobilize with PT when stable.
Repeat CBC and BMP in AM. Vasopressors if MAP persistently under 65 despite fluid - notify attending.
Full code per daughter and prior documentation. Attending notified, will see patient this morning.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD2 Morning
lines: Subjective:
Pt slept in intervals overnight, more interactive this morning, knows daughter and says she is in the hospital.
No chills overnight. Took sips of water and half a cup of broth.
Overnight Events:
Weaned to 3L NC at 06:00 with SpO2 94%. Respiratory rate 20 this AM, down from 30 on arrival.
MAP maintained 68-74 after additional 500 mL NS at 07:20, no norepinephrine required.
Vitals:
T 37.4 C, HR 96, BP 104/60, RR 20, SpO2 94% on 3L. UOP 780 mL last 24 hr.
Labs:
WBC 9,800, platelets 96,000, creatinine 2.1 mg/dL, HCO3 21, K 4.0.
Lactate 1.9 this AM.
Blood culture and urine culture pending at this time.
Exam:
Gen: more alert, no distress. Card: RRR. Pulm: clear. Abd: soft, minimal suprapubic tenderness. Ext: no edema.
Neuro: oriented to self and place, attention improved.
Assessment/Plan:
Sepsis from urinary source - improving. Hemodynamics stabilized with fluids alone.
AKI - improving, creatinine down from 2.6. Continue to hold ACE inhibitor, avoid nephrotoxins.
Thrombocytopenia - consumptive, trending up, no bleeding.
Transitioned to oral cephalexin this morning.
Wean O2 as tolerated. PT eval today. Encourage PO intake. Repeat labs in AM.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD4
lines: Subjective:
Pt reports feeling much better, ate full breakfast, ambulated 40 feet in hallway with walker and PT.
No fever, no dysuria, denies dizziness on standing.
Events:
Blood culture positive for E. coli at 30 hours; susceptibilities show sensitivity to cephalosporins.
Off supplemental O2 since HD3 at 14:00, SpO2 95-96% on room air.
Vitals:
T 36.9 C, HR 78, BP 122/68, RR 17, SpO2 96% RA. UOP 1,450 mL last 24 hr.
Labs:
WBC 7,400, platelets 168,000, creatinine 1.1 mg/dL, Na 138, K 4.2, HCO3 25.
Exam:
Gen: comfortable, sitting up in chair. Card: RRR, no murmur. Pulm: clear bilaterally.
Abd: soft, nontender. Ext: no edema. Skin intact.
Neuro: alert and oriented to person, place, time, and situation. Back to baseline per daughter.
Assessment/Plan:
Sepsis, urinary source, E. coli bacteremia - resolved clinically, afebrile 48 hr.
Continue oral antibiotic to complete course, total 10 days from initiation.
AKI - near resolution. Restart lisinopril at discharge if creatinine remains stable and BP tolerates.
Thrombocytopenia - resolved.
Delirium - resolved.
PT recommends home with daughter check-ins, no SNF needed.
Anticipate discharge tomorrow if stable overnight. Daughter updated at 10:15.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - Sepsis, E. coli Urinary Source
lines: Discharge Diagnosis: Sepsis secondary to urinary tract infection with E. coli bacteremia.
Secondary: Acute kidney injury, thrombocytopenia, acute hypoxemic respiratory distress, acute encephalopathy - all resolved.
Length of Stay: HD1 through HD5.
Hospital Course:
87 yo female presented with confusion and chills. Daughter reports patient normally independent and oriented; on arrival confused, oriented to self only, GCS 13.
Temperature 37.9 C at triage; WBC 11,200. Respiratory rate 30; SpO2 88% on RA, placed on 6L NC with SpO2 93%.
Lactate 4.2 mmol/L at 02:10, 3.6 mmol/L repeat at 05:30.
Received 2.5 L normal saline bolus (30 mL/kg); BP after bolus 86/48, MAP 61.
Post-bolus vitals at 04:45: HR 118, BP 88/50, RR 26, T 38.9 C.
Norepinephrine discussed by ED team for MAP 64; held after additional fluid with MAP 68.
Urinalysis with large leukocyte esterase and more than 50 WBC per high power field; blood culture x2 and urine culture drawn at 02:20 before antibiotics.
Ceftriaxone 1 g IV given at 04:30 as the only antibiotic dose; transitioned to oral cephalexin the next morning.
Blood culture positive for E. coli at 30 hours, pan sensitive. Urine culture with same organism.
Creatinine 2.6 mg/dL (baseline 0.9 mg/dL); platelets 84,000 on admission.
Creatinine improved to 1.1 and platelets to 168,000 by HD4 with volume resuscitation and source control.
Oxygen weaned off by HD3, mental status returned to baseline by HD4 per daughter.
Discharge Vitals: T 36.8 C, HR 76, BP 118/66, RR 16, SpO2 96% on room air.
Discharge Exam: alert, oriented x4, lungs clear, abdomen soft nontender, ambulates with walker.
Discharge Medications:
Cephalexin 500 mg PO q8h to complete 10 day total course.
Amlodipine 5 mg daily resumed. Lisinopril 10 mg daily resumed at discharge, creatinine stable.
Atorvastatin 20 mg nightly, vitamin D 1000 units daily, acetaminophen 650 mg PRN.
Discharge Instructions:
Drink at least 6 glasses of fluid daily. Do not use NSAIDs.
Return for fever above 38.0 C, confusion, decreased urination, dizziness, or inability to keep fluids down.
Home PT twice weekly x 2 weeks, walker for all ambulation.
Follow Up:
Primary care in 5 to 7 days for BMP to confirm renal recovery and BP check.
Discharged HD5 at 13:20 in stable condition, home with daughter. Daughter verbalized understanding of instructions.
